## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bilārakosiyajātaka* (Ja 450) is a narrative belonging to the Pali *Jātaka* collection. According to the frame story, the Buddha delivered this tale while residing at Jetavana about a monk who was zealously devoted to giving. In the story of the past, the Bodhisattva was reborn as Śakra (Sakka), the king of the gods, while his future chief disciples Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana appeared alongside him as the moon god and the sun god, respectively [Powers 2009].

 Resembling parallels are also noted in the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G3-Dhp 41–50), Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* collections (UV 5, UVS 5, Uv Kg 5; T 212, T 213), Chinese Dharmapada recensions (T 210), and several suttas in the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 3.4, SN 3.20, SN 3.22) and *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5.36).

These thematic and textual links are corroborated by DharmaNexus text-reuse data, which records 43 Pali-internal matching segments across eight texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial verse reuse occurs with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Devatā Saṁyutta* (specifically matching SN 1.32 at §8.1–10.6), the *Devaputta Saṁyutta* (SN 2.23), *Duddadajātaka* (Ja 180), *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547), and the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies cross-language reuse alignments with the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100), the Tibetan *Tridharmaka-nāma-sūtra* (D0253), the *Puṇyabala-avadāna* (D0347), and the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (D4099, D0326) [DharmaNexus].
